summary: Both sides are a static, uniform chartreuse fill whose single 'LightsOn' slider lights an exactly matching leading fraction of the strip; the only divergence is a small constant hue offset (orig RGB 204,255,0 vs port 173,255,0).
observations: Static, non-animated on both sides: motion 0 and motionLit 0 on every captured frame of the 6 s/20 fps baseline (120 frames) and the 60 s/5 fps survey (300 frames); meanBrightness is a flat 153 (orig) / 143 (port) with brightnessTrend 'steady' and zeroMotionFrames = all frames on both. A --skip 600 --seconds 4 run renders byte-identical output to t=0, so there is no slow drift, no mode rotation and no warm-up transient on either side.

Untouched, every pixel of the strip carries one identical colour on each side: orig = (204,255,0) at all 60 px, port = (173,255,0) at all 60 px (--dump at 0 s, 3 s, 5.9 s). That is HSV hue 0.200 vs 0.220 at full saturation/value — the port is ~7 degrees greener/less yellow. It is the pattern's ONLY visual content besides the dial, but both read as chartreuse and the difference is only obvious side by side.

The colour is pixel-count- and rig-independent on both sides and by the same amount: at --pixels 12, --pixels 600 and --rig grid --grid 8x8 every pixel is still exactly (204,255,0) orig / (173,255,0) port. No gradient, no per-pixel variation anywhere.

The 'LightsOn' slider is not a brightness dimmer — it lights a contiguous leading run of pixels and leaves the rest at exact black (0,0,0), and the lit pixels keep full-value colour. Lit counts on a 60 px strip agree exactly on both sides at every value tested: 0 -> 0 lit (all black), 0.02 -> 2, 0.25 -> 15, 0.5 -> 30, 0.75 -> 45, 0.9 -> 54, 1.0 -> 60. The lit run always starts at pixel index 0 on both sides, so there is no mirroring or off-by-one in the port's indexing, and even the rounding at the edges matches.

Control surface matches exactly: both sides expose one control, name 'sliderLightsOn', kind 'slider', label 'LightsOn'. Neither side binds sensor globals (wantsSensors false on both), and neither reports a compile or runtime error.

probe.json agrees on the dial's shape and near-linearity on both sides: deltas 0 -> 153.00 (orig) / 142.67 (port), 0.5 -> 76.5 / 71.33, 1 -> 0.00 / 0.00. Delta 0 at value 1 on both sides means the untouched default state is equivalent to the slider fully up, i.e. all pixels on.

Rendering at 5, 20 and 40 fps produces the same constant image on both sides (identical mean brightness and identical dumped pixels), so frame-rate coupling is not applicable here; seeds 1, 7 and 1234 also render identically on both sides, consistent with a pattern that uses no randomness.

dials.name: sliderLightsOn
dials.origEffect: Lights a contiguous leading fraction of the strip: value v lights round(v*N) pixels starting at index 0 at full colour (204,255,0), the rest exact black. 0 = whole strip black, 1 = whole strip lit (identical to the untouched default). Measured lit counts on 60 px: 0/2/15/30/45/54/60 at v = 0/0.02/0.25/0.5/0.75/0.9/1.
dials.portEffect: Identical mechanism and identical lit counts at every value tested (0/2/15/30/45/54/60), same contiguous run starting at index 0, same exact-black off pixels — only the lit colour differs, (173,255,0) instead of (204,255,0).

feedback: Only one thing to fix: the base colour. The original fills the strip with HSV hue 0.200 (RGB 204,255,0); the port fills it with hue 0.220 (RGB 173,255,0). Shift the port's hue down by 0.02 so its lit pixels come out at exactly (204,255,0) at full brightness.

Everything else is already correct and should not be touched: the flat single-colour fill with no per-pixel or per-frame variation, the exact-black off pixels, and the slider's leading-run semantics with matching rounding (2 lit at 0.02, 54 at 0.9 on a 60 px strip).
